name: Missouri Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
notes: Researched from public dor.mo.gov and mytax.mo.gov pages only (no login, no form submitted). MyTax Missouri: Member Sign In with User ID and Password (Forgot User ID? / Forgot password?); New User? Register Here, then register as an Administrator of the individual income tax account using information from the most recently filed return; a PIN is mailed to the address on file to finish registration (prior filing history required; not expressible). Registration form asks for first and last name, phone and email to create a user ID. Password policy: at least 15 characters meeting 3 of 4 complexity rules (upper, lower, number, special); expires every 90 days (expiry not expressible). Public links: Make an individual tax payment as a guest; Request a Payment Plan; Check Payment Status. Fees (NCR Payments, kept by the vendor): e-check $0.50; card 2.0% + $0.25 per transaction (engine charges 2.0%; the 25-cent fixed part is in fees.notes, see cross-owner request on fixed+percent fees); NCR may charge $25 for an insufficient-funds or closed-account debit. Posting: e-check 3-4 business days, card 5-6. Pay by phone 888-929-0513. Mail: MO-1040V with check to PO Box 385, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0385. Payment plans: Internet Installment Agreement request on MyTax Missouri (SSN, the most recent notice including its PIN, bank account or credit card); questions 573-751-7200 or income@dor.mo.gov; interest and additions to tax continue. Additions: failure to pay 5%; failure to file 5% a month up to 25%. No recurring AutoPay for a balance (inferred); scheduling and cancel rules are not published on the pages read (family defaults kept).

help.title: Pay your Missouri individual income tax
paragraphs: Pay online by e-check from a checking or savings account or by MasterCard, Discover, Visa or American Express. You can pay as a guest or after you sign in to MyTax Missouri. Payments are processed by the vendor NCR Payments, and the convenience fees go to the vendor, not the Department.

An e-check costs $0.50 and posts in 3 to 4 business days. A card payment costs 2.0% plus $0.25 per transaction and posts in 5 to 6 business days. The vendor may charge $25 if an e-check is returned for insufficient funds or a closed account.

You can also pay by e-check or card by calling 888-929-0513, or mail a check or money order payable to the Missouri Department of Revenue with Form MO-1040V to PO Box 385, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0385. Do not postdate the check.

help.title: Payment plan agreements
paragraphs: If you cannot pay in full, request an individual payment plan with the Internet Installment Agreement request on MyTax Missouri (Request a Payment Plan).

Before you start, have your Social Security number, your most recent tax notice including its PIN, and your bank account information or a credit card. Payment plans are not offered for motor vehicle sales tax or driver license fees.
Interest and additions to tax still apply to unpaid tax while you pay. Questions: call 573-751-7200 or email income@dor.mo.gov.

help.title: Register for MyTax Missouri
paragraphs: Sign in to MyTax Missouri with your User ID and password. To register, choose New User? Register Here under the sign-in box and register as an Administrator of your individual income tax account, using information from your most recently filed return. You need a prior filing history with the Department.
A PIN is then mailed to the address on file. When it arrives, sign in to finish registering.
Passwords must be at least 15 characters and meet 3 of 4 rules: an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character. Passwords expire every 90 days.

help.title: Additions to tax and interest
paragraphs: An extension to file is not an extension to pay. Tax not paid by the due date gets an addition to tax of 5% of the unpaid balance for failure to pay, and simple interest accrues on delinquent tax.
Not filing on time adds 5% of the unpaid balance for each month, up to 25%. Paying any part of the tax before the due date reduces these amounts.
